title: KV cache migrations and runtime state migration playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview:
This playbook describes a safe, repeatable process for migrating runtime state for private deployments of the Redwood inference runtime, with a primary focus on KV cache migrations (prefix/KV cache) and associated runtime in-memory state changes. It is intended for SREs and Platform Operators performing upgrades, model variant rollouts, or hardware maintenance that require moving or invalidating cached state across nodes or model variants.

Scope:
- Applies to VPC and on-prem private deployments managed by Redwood Private control plane where runtime KV cache is used to accelerate token serving.
- Covers deterministic migration patterns, live invalidation, warm-start strategies, and rollback procedures.
- Excludes: model weight migration (handled by model-onboarding), HSM/KMS key rotation, and physical hardware replacement procedures.

Goals and acceptance criteria (SLOs):
- Migration completion without increasing 99th percentile tail latency above baseline + 50ms for more than 5 minutes.
- No more than 0.5% increase in error rate (5xx) during steady-state within 30 minutes post-migration.
- No data-loss of persisted KV entries (persisted store must remain consistent).

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments SRE (oncall-sre@redwood.example.com)
- Backup owner: runtime-team (runtime-ops@redwood.example.com)
- Rollout approver: Release Manager (release-manager@redwood.example.com)

Prerequisites and environment checklist (table):
| Item | Required value / action | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valid control plane connection | API token (role=deploy) and network access to customer control plane | Operator |
| Backup of persisted cache store | Snapshot created within last 30m and stored in object storage | Operator |
| Canary capacity | At least 2 spare GPU instances with compatible model artifact | SRE |
| Monitoring & tracing | Grafana dashboard + traces for request_id routing enabled | Observability team |
| Runbook accessible | This playbook loaded into the incident response tool | Operator |

Pre-migration safety checks (execute before any live action):
1) Verify persisted-store snapshot:
   - Command: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-backups/{deployment}/kv-snapshots/ --recursive | grep $(date -d '1 hour ago' +%Y-%m-%d)
   - Confirm snapshot size within expected range (no sudden shrinkage).
2) Confirm control-plane policy and quotas are available:
   - CLI: rwdctl deployments describe --id <DEPLOYMENT_ID> --fields quotas
3) Confirm canaries and health checks:
   - There must be a successful smoke test run in the last 15 minutes (see Post-migration validation section).
4) Confirm traffic routing policy and fallback targets are configured:
   - Ensure a warm-fallback model variant exists (fallback_model: <model-id>-quantized)

Recommended migration strategies (choose one based on risk tolerance):
- Invalidate-and-rewarm (fast): invalidate KV entries on target nodes and let live traffic rebuild cache. Use when lost cache is acceptable and latency SLOs have cushion.
- Live-merge with prefix routing (safe): route a percentage of traffic to new nodes while selectively replaying persisted-key prefixes to warm caches. Best for large persisted stores.
- Drained restart + replay (conservative): drain node, snapshot persisted store, restart runtime with new binary/config, replay keys from snapshot to warmed nodes.

Step-by-step migration procedure (Live-merge with prefix routing — recommended default):
1) Prepare canary nodes:
   - Provision 2 canary GPU nodes in the target AZ with the new runtime or config.
   - Label nodes: rwd-role=canary, rwd-version=<target-version>.
2) Snapshot persisted store:
   - rwdctl kv snapshot create --deployment <DEPLOYMENT_ID> --output s3://redwood-backups/{deployment}/kv-snapshots/{ts}.json
   - Confirm checksum: rwdctl kv snapshot verify --path s3://.../{ts}.json
3) Start read-only warmers on canary nodes:
   - Deploy the warmers with settings: parallelism=4, target-prefixes-file=/opt/prefixes/to-replay.txt
   - Example systemd unit: [Service]
     ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rwd-warm --snapshot s3://.../{ts}.json --mode=replay --threads=4
4) Begin phased traffic routing (percentages are examples):
   - Phase A: 5% traffic to canary for 15 minutes. Monitor latency and error rates.
   - Phase B: 20% traffic for 15 minutes. If metrics stable, continue.
   - Phase C: 50% traffic for 10 minutes. Verify warmed hit-rate for prefixes > 70%.
   - Phase D: 100% traffic to new nodes, decommission old nodes.
5) Validate post-traffic metrics (see Observability queries).

Rollback procedure (fast fallback):
1) Immediately reroute traffic to previous pool using control-plane policy:
   - rwdctl routing set --deployment <DEPLOYMENT_ID> --pool previous --priority 100
2) If routing command fails, disable canary nodes at the load-balancer level and re-enable previous nodes.
3) Restore persisted-store from snapshot if corruption is detected:
   - rwdctl kv snapshot restore --path s3://.../{ts}.json --force --deployment <DEPLOYMENT_ID>
4) Open an incident and tag the migration ticket for a postmortem.

Automated safety guards and health checks (what to watch in the first 30 minutes):
- Latency SLI: prometheus query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="runtime"}[2m])) by (le))
- Error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime",status=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="runtime"}[1m]))
- Cache hit ratio by node: rate(kv_cache_hits_total[1m]) / (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[1m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses_total[1m]))
- Slow-start guard: if 99th latency > baseline + 50ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows, automatically roll traffic back to previous pool.

Post-migration validation (automated + manual):
- Automated smoke-tests (must pass within 5 minutes):
  1) token-generation correctness check: curl -s -X POST https://{endpoint}/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello, world"}' | jq .status
  2) trace sanity: check KV read traces exist for a sample request_id using tracing UI or jaeger query.
- Manual checks (operator):
  - Run load test at 10% of expected peak for 10 minutes and review 95/99 latency bands.
  - Verify billing/tokens counters to ensure no double-counting anomalies.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Cold cache spike: Acceptable for brief window; if tail latency breach persists > 5m, perform rollback and rewarm offline snapshot.
- Persisted store mismatch: Restore from snapshot and run key reconciliation tool: rwdctl kv reconcile --source s3://.../{ts}.json --target /var/lib/rwd/kv --dry-run
- Compatibility errors after binary upgrade: Rollback code path and open urgent model-onboarding ticket with runtime team.

Runbook snippets and command reference:
- Create snapshot:
  rwdctl kv snapshot create --deployment DEPLOYMENT_ID --output s3://redwood-backups/DEPLOYMENT_ID/kv-snapshots/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json
- Verify snapshot checksum:
  rwdctl kv snapshot verify --path s3://redwood-backups/DEPLOYMENT_ID/kv-snapshots/<ts>.json
- Route traffic to pool:
  rwdctl routing set --deployment DEPLOYMENT_ID --pool <POOL_NAME> --percent 20

Configuration knobs worth tuning prior to migration:
- warmers.parallelism (default 4) — increases replay throughput; higher values increase temporary I/O load.
- cache.eviction.window (default 60s) — shorten to aggressively evict stale prefixes before migration when desired.
- routing.ramp_step (default 5%) — smaller steps reduce risk but increase time.

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- For every migration > 5 minutes of SLO breach, create a postmortem with: timeline, metric graphs, root-cause, remediation, and action owner. Attach snapshots and runbook notes.
- Maintain a migration playbook index in the shared SRE wiki and link results back to the customer deployment page.

Appendix A — Example warm-replay YAML:
---
warm_replay:
  snapshot_s3: "s3://redwood-backups/DEPLOYMENT_ID/kv-snapshots/20250218T120000Z.json"
  threads: 4
  prefixes_file: "/opt/prefixes/to-replay.txt"
  mode: "replay"
---

Appendix B — Troubleshooting quick checklist:
- If snapshot restore fails, check S3 permissions and re-run rwdctl with --assume-role.
- If warmers are CPU bound, reduce parallelism and increase warm window.
- If routing rollback repeatedly flaps, quarantine the canary nodes and open a CAPA with runtime-team.
